newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Analysts unsure worst over for Totta.
newsitem.headline: Analysts unsure worst over for Totta.

text.p: Shares in Banco Totta & Acores slumped another five percent on Thursday to 2,435 escudos ($14.90) but analysts were divided on whether the worst was now over for the stock.
The share was off earlier lows of 2,365 escudos.

"I think that the stock could go significantly lower, knowing the attitude of the foreign investor who, when he wants out, does not pay much attention to the price," said Nuno Thomaz of brokers Titulo-Sociedade Corretora.
"It is going to be difficult for Totta to return to its previous levels (above 3,000 escudos)," he said.

Investors have hammered the bank's stock since it announced lower than expected results and dividend payment last Friday, driving the price down 26 percent in four sessions. Turnover has reached 60 billion escudos, equal to five percent of capital.
The decline has taken the bank back to lows hit at the end of 1995 when it reached 2,330 escudos.
But some traders felt that the selling had been overdone.
"Totta has fallen too far. At these levels it is a good buy," said Joao Capucho of Banco Finantia. "Below 2,400 escudos, it becomes an interesting stock from a trading point of view," he added.
"But there are a couple of big foreign players who are selling because they do not like the lack of transparency," the analyst said.
Analysts said that Banco Totta had led the market to expect a signficantly better performance, with most forecasts looking for a dividend of 180-190 escudos, in line with the 1995 payout.
Capucho said that the end-year results, with the bank declaring a net profit of 15 billion escudos against 17.2 billion in 1995, pointed to a loss of 1.5 billion escudos in the last quarter.
Totta had posted a profit over the first nine months of 16.7 billion escudos.
"It is this (loss) that is penalising the stock strongly, more than the dividend," Capucho added.
"After the heavy selling by foreign investors is over, Totta will recover because the present fall in the share price shows signs of panic," said one trader.
Another said: "Even if the bank keeps a dividend of 135 escudos, the present share price around 2,400 escudos gives a dividend yield of 5.6 percent which is very good for any bank."
He added: "Once this storm is over, Totta will recover, although not to previous levels around 3,300 escudos."
